briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Rescheduling Momentum Builds Nationally While Michigan Operators Eye Tax Relief and New Storefronts
briefs.top: Federal rescheduling cleared another milestone this week as DEA released its full hearing transcript and final briefs, while in Michigan, GOP gubernatorial nominee John James and state lawmakers are pushing hard to unwind the 24% wholesale tax even as new stores keep opening across metro Detroit and Ann Arbor.

local.text: Lume Cannabis Co. opened a new Ann Arbor storefront at 2247 W. Liberty Street, with a three-day grand opening event running 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Common Citizen is set to open a new dispensary in Eastpointe after reaching a court-approved deal giving it until Dec. 1 to renovate and start selling, adding a second shop to a town that currently has only one.

Michigan GOP gubernatorial nominee John James pledged to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale marijuana tax as part of his campaign platform, arguing the levy "drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections."

State Rep. James DeSana filed HB 6224 to repeal the 24% wholesale tax outright, following an earlier Senate repeal bill from Sen. Jonathan Lindsey that already drew seven cosponsors including three Democrats — signs of building bipartisan appetite for relief.

The wholesale tax has pushed average flower prices to a record-low $58 an ounce and continues to squeeze margins, but the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's constitutional challenge is still alive on appeal, keeping a legal path to relief open for operators.

national.text: The DEA submitted its final briefs supporting cannabis rescheduling, with the agency citing HHS and FDA research showing accepted medical uses for treating anorexia, pain, and nausea as the core reason marijuana can't remain Schedule I.

The DEA released the full official transcript of its rescheduling hearing, with government lawyers arguing marijuana "can no longer remain in Schedule I," while NIDA Director Nora Volkow said rescheduling will reduce barriers to research.

The FDA finalized its clinical-trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and will hold a September 14 public hearing on therapeutic psychedelic use, building the regulatory infrastructure for what could become a live approval pathway.

Curaleaf is pressing a hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis directly to shareholders after the two sides traded public accusations, with Aurora touting 17% year-over-year growth in its international medical cannabis business as it fends off the offer.
Illinois expanded its medical cannabis program, adding sickle cell disease and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome with chronic pain as new qualifying conditions.
